official.description_text:
Researcher in intelligent building and thermal energy systems
Apply for position
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Architecture and Built Environment
Job description
We seek a researcher to develop intelligent heating and cooling systems for buildings and district energy networks using physics-based and data-driven models, advanced control and optimization. The work covers HVAC systems, heat pumps, thermal storage, district heating and cooling, and renewable and recovered energy. Tasks include developing and validating models and digital twins, analyzing measured and simulated data, and assessing energy efficiency, flexibility, emissions, indoor environmental quality and climate resilience, including overheating. The researcher will conduct independent studies, publish results, prepare funding applications and collaborate with academic partners, industry and public authorities. Teaching and supervision may be included.
Qualifications
Requirements
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree
Documented research expertise in building energy systems, thermal energy systems, building services engineering, energy engineering or related fields, demonstrated through scientific publications.
Experience in modeling and simulation of energy systems and analysis of numerical or measured data.
Experience in control, optimization, or data-driven methods relevant to heating and cooling systems.
Ability to plan and conduct research independently and collaborate in interdisciplinary projects.
Very good oral and written communication skills in English, since the position involves scientific publication and international collaboration.
Preferred qualifications
Experience in model predictive control, reinforcement learning, physics-informed optimization or digital twins.
Knowledge of heat pumps, thermal storage, recovered and renewable energy, and district heating and cooling.
Programming in Python, MATLAB, or similar, and use of simulation tools such as IDA ICE, TRNSYS, or EnergyPlus.
Experience validating models or control strategies using measurements from real facilities.
Knowledge of overheating, climate adaptation, thermal comfort and indoor environmental quality.
Demonstrated teaching ability and experience in teaching, supervision or research communication.
Experience in research leadership, funding applications, collaboration and practical uptake of research results.
Knowledge of diversity and equal opportunities, particularly gender equality.
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Join us at KTH
KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. Equality, diversity and equal opportunities are essential to quality and form an integral part of KTH’s core values as a university and public authority.
Learn more about our benefits and what it's like to work and grow at KTH

To apply for the position
Log into KTH's recruitment system in order to apply for this position. You are responsible to ensure that your application is complete according to the instructions in the ad.
The application must include:
CV including relevant professional experience, expertise and a list of publications.
Copy of diplomas and grades from your previous university studies. Translations into English or Swedish if the original documents have not been issued in any of these languages.
Brief account of why you want to conduct research, your academic interests and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. Max two pages long.
Your complete application must be received by KTH no later than the last day of application, midnight CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).
About the employment
The employment is valid until further notice (permanent post) according to agreement.
The employment begins with a six-month probationary period.

ai.summary: Researcher position (permanent, full-time) at KTH developing physics-based and data-driven models, advanced control, and optimization for intelligent building and district energy systems (HVAC, heat pumps, thermal storage). Work includes modeling, digital twins, simulation, analysis, and validation against real facility measurements.

thematic_fit.rationale: Position is in building energy systems engineering and thermal systems control. Researcher's domain is human-centred XR, spatial cognition, collaborative learning, and immersive systems design. No thematic overlap. Posting mentions 'indoor environmental quality' and 'thermal comfort,' but as building physics metrics, not human factors or user experience topics.

methodological_fit.rationale: Position requires physics-based modeling (IDA ICE, TRNSYS, EnergyPlus), data-driven methods (Python, MATLAB), model predictive control, optimization, and validation against measured facility data. Researcher has intermediate quantitative research and experimental design skills, but no background in building energy systems, control theory, HVAC, thermal storage, or these simulation tools. Programming is in C#/Unity for game logic, not scientific Python for energy modeling.

growth_value.rationale: Learning building energy systems and thermal engineering would not close gaps aligned with target identity (human-centred immersive systems, spatial learning, collaborative XR). Position emphasizes technical modeling and control—areas distant from researcher's core strengths (HCI evaluation, user studies, collaborative design). Does not advance capability in human-centred research methodology.

strategic_value.rationale: KTH is strong; Stockholm meets geographic preference. However, position is permanent researcher track in building systems, not pathway to doctoral studies or HCI research. No connection to target institutions (Aalto, TU Delft) or to research groups working on spatial learning or immersive systems. Researcher would be embedded in building/energy engineering community, not HCI or XR networks. Unclear how permanent role in building physics advances target identity.

eligibility_flags: Position requires doctoral degree (researcher has MSc by Research in progress—degree must be conferred before application).

Position explicitly requires 'documented research expertise in building energy systems, thermal energy systems, building services engineering, energy engineering or related fields, demonstrated through scientific publications.' Researcher's publication record is in XR/HCI (one first-author journal article, one SMR in progress)—may not satisfy this requirement.
Security clearance may be required per Swedish Protective Security Act (ambiguous).
risks: Fundamental domain mismatch: no background in building energy, thermal systems, HVAC, or control engineering.

Position emphasizes independent research leadership, funding applications, and teaching—but researcher would be entering an unfamiliar field without established expertise or publication record in building systems.
Permanent position is long-term commitment to building engineering; difficult to pivot later to HCI/XR research.
No human subjects, user evaluation, or design component—misaligned with researcher's methodological identity and strengths.
Joining building/energy engineering group would isolate researcher from HCI and XR communities.
Publication record (XR/HCI) does not build credibility in building energy domain; would require substantial re-establishing of research reputation.
Position involves teaching and supervision in energy systems—outside researcher's current expertise.
